title: A fresh look at a classic deep field
caption: The MIRI Deep Imaging Survey field in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, G. Östlin, P. G. Perez-Gonzalez, J. Melinder, the JADES Collaboration, the MIDIS collaboration, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb)

recognition.text: Ranked #37 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Thousands of galaxies of many shapes and sizes crowd a black background, most of them circles or ovals, a few spirals, the farthest shrunk to dots. This is part of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, revisited by Webb in the region known as the MIRI Deep Imaging Survey, or MIDIS.

Webb's Mid-Infrared Instrument observed it through its three shortest-wavelength filters for nearly 100 hours in total, including Webb's longest look at an extragalactic field in a single filter so far. Combined with NIRCam data, the view turned up over 2500 sources in this small patch of sky, including hundreds of extremely red galaxies that may be massive and dust-shrouded, or mature systems whose stars formed early.

Color tells astronomers about each galaxy. Orange and red ones give off extra long-wavelength light, from dust, heavy star formation or an active nucleus. Small greenish-white galaxies are especially distant. Most appear blue and cyan, brightest at shorter near-infrared wavelengths.

understand.summary: Webb's MIRI and NIRCam data are combined. Blue and cyan show near-infrared light, white and green the peak mid-infrared wavelengths, and orange and red the longest mid-infrared wavelengths.
understand.eye: All of this light is infrared and invisible to the human eye.

explore: Webb's sharp resolution, even in the mid-infrared, lets researchers make out the shapes of many of these galaxies and examine how their light is distributed, which helps explain how they grew. The MIRI observations were part of Webb programs #1283 and #6511.
alt: A deep field of thousands of galaxies on black, mostly small circles and ovals with a few spirals, some glowing red and orange.
